meta.label: Lupus nephritis patient journey
notes: Chronological clinical arc for SLE / lupus nephritis, anchored to the moments patients describe rather than the chapters clinicians use.
Trial-related stages (6-8) are weighted toward CAR-T because that's the corpus we have. The taxonomy still applies to other trial-considered therapies; rename steps when a richer corpus arrives.
Includes UCTD/MCTD adjacent voices in the corpus; their early stages (1-2) are similar enough that this taxonomy covers them with light reinterpretation.
Replace with corpus-driven taxonomy (see feature_backlog 'Corpus-driven journey-stage taxonomy') when that pipeline lands.

stages.label: Pre-diagnosis
stages.description: Before lupus is named. Fatigue, joint pain, edema, rashes, kidney symptoms — speakers reach for explanations, often dismissed by clinicians for years.

steps.label: Symptom onset
steps.description: First noticing something is wrong. Often non-specific (fatigue, pain) and easily attributable to other causes.

steps.label: Seeking answers
steps.description: Repeated PCP visits, online research, advocacy from family / patient communities to be taken seriously.

steps.label: Pre-diagnosis uncertainty
steps.description: Living without a name for what's happening; navigating uncertainty about whether this is permanent.

stages.label: Diagnostic odyssey
stages.description: Bouncing through PCP → rheumatology → nephrology. ANA / dsDNA labs, kidney workup, biopsy for classification (Class III, IV, V LN). The point where lupus becomes the named diagnosis.

steps.label: Specialist bouncing
steps.description: Referral cascade between primary care and rheumatology / nephrology; often delayed by months.

steps.label: Kidney workup
steps.description: Bloodwork, urine protein, imaging — the steps that escalate suspicion to a biopsy decision.

steps.label: Biopsy and classification
steps.description: Kidney biopsy and the moment of getting an LN class assignment (III, IV, V), which sets the treatment intensity.

stages.label: Induction treatment
stages.description: First-line aggressive immunosuppression to stop active inflammation. High-dose steroids + cyclophosphamide or mycophenolate (CellCept), often with rituximab or anifrolumab.

steps.label: Starting induction
steps.description: First weeks on high-dose steroids + chemotherapy / biologic; logistic shock of infusions and side effects.

steps.label: Induction side effects
steps.description: Steroid weight gain, mood changes, infection risk, infusion reactions; quality-of-life trough.

steps.label: Induction response
steps.description: Labs improving, protein dropping; first signs the treatment is working (or not).

stages.label: Stable maintenance
stages.description: Long-term immunosuppression to hold remission. Plaquenil + lower-dose immunosuppressant + tapered steroids. Lifestyle adapted around medication schedule and infection avoidance.

steps.label: Long-term immunosuppression
steps.description: Daily medication regimen settled; infusions on schedule; labs every 1-3 months.

steps.label: Lifestyle adjustments
steps.description: Sun avoidance, infection precautions, exercise modifications, navigating fatigue around work / family.

steps.label: Monitoring routine
steps.description: Regular nephrologist / rheumatologist visits, lab monitoring, watching for early flare signs.

stages.label: Flare / refractory cycle
stages.description: Disease returns despite maintenance. New flare or recognition that current therapy is failing. Drug switching, retreatment with induction, accumulating treatment fatigue.

steps.label: Flare recognition
steps.description: Symptoms or labs signal active disease return; clinical confirmation of relapse.

steps.label: Drug switching
steps.description: Trying a new biologic / immunosuppressant (Gazyva, anifrolumab, voclosporin, rituximab); hope-then-disappointment cycles.

steps.label: Treatment fatigue
steps.description: Cumulative burden of years of immunosuppression, infusions, side effects; questioning whether the current path is sustainable.

stages.label: Trial consideration
stages.description: Exploring CAR-T or other novel therapies. Reading the German study, searching ClinicalTrials.gov, talking to community, working out eligibility, weighing logistical / financial / personal cost.

steps.label: Trial awareness
steps.description: Hearing about CAR-T-for-lupus (German Erlangen study, Fate, BMS, etc.) through community or clinician; initial reading.

steps.label: Eligibility self-assessment
steps.description: Working out whether one's disease severity, prior therapies, comorbidities, and geography qualify for a given trial.

steps.label: Logistical assessment
steps.description: Travel to site, time off work, caregiver availability, post-infusion proximity requirements, insurance / cost — the practical blockers.

steps.label: Consent or decline
steps.description: The decision moment — sign on, defer, or decline. Often shaped by family situation more than medical reasoning.

stages.label: In-trial experience
stages.description: Active treatment phase. Apheresis / cell collection, lymphodepleting chemotherapy, infusion, hospitalization for acute monitoring (CRS, ICANS, infection).

steps.label: Cell collection
steps.description: Apheresis / leukapheresis to harvest T cells; weeks of waiting for engineered cells to be manufactured.

steps.label: Lymphodepletion
steps.description: Conditioning chemotherapy (usually fludarabine + cyclophosphamide) to prepare for the CAR-T infusion.

steps.label: Infusion and hospitalization
steps.description: The actual cell infusion (often a quick procedure), followed by inpatient monitoring; staying near the center for 30 days post-infusion.

steps.label: Acute complications
steps.description: Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity (ICANS), infections — the high-stakes side-effect window.

stages.label: Post-trial
stages.description: After acute recovery. Off all immunosuppression (the headline outcome), slow return to baseline, long-term follow-up for safety + durability of remission. Re-integrating identity around 'in remission' or 'cured.'

steps.label: Short-term recovery
steps.description: First weeks-to-months home; gradual return to work / normal life; vigilant follow-up for relapse signs.

steps.label: Off immunosuppression
steps.description: The unfamiliar state of no daily lupus medication; reframing identity from chronic patient toward something new.

steps.label: Long-term follow-up
steps.description: Years-out monitoring for delayed effects, B-cell repopulation, secondary autoimmunity, durability of remission.
